stories.headline: Russian drone strikes Ukraine's SBU headquarters in Kyiv as US envoys prepare peace mission
stories.body:
A Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security services in Kyiv on Friday [c4]. The attack injured at least 12 people, according to Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko [c4]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Moscow of directly targeting the personal office of the SBU chief during the daytime strike [c8]. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga described the strike on the SBU central building on Volodymyrska Street as a major escalation [c9].

The acting head of the SBU, Oleksandr Poklad, was not inside the building during the attack and was unharmed [c10]. This was the first time the SBU headquarters had been hit since Russia began its full-scale invasion in February 2022 [c11, c14]. Russia currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory [c14].

The strike occurred as United States envoys prepared to travel to the region [c1]. US President Donald Trump announced on Friday that special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are traveling to Kyiv and Moscow to present a proposal aimed at ending the war [c1]. Russian state news agency TASS reported that Witkoff and Kushner will visit Moscow on Saturday and Sunday [c2]. Zelenskyy said that the envoys will visit Ukraine on Sunday [c3]. This trip marks their first journey to Ukraine since Trump returned to power [c3].

Zelenskyy proposed a temporary ceasefire during the visits of Witkoff and Kushner [c7]. He said that Ukraine would conduct no airstrikes if Russia agrees to a ceasefire during the peace talks [c12]. Zelenskyy also confirmed that Ukraine agreed to keep Russian airspace operating normally so the US envoys can travel safely [c15].

On Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin spoke at an international economic forum [c13]. Putin said that there are chances for a peace deal [c13]. But he maintained his demands for territorial concessions from Ukraine [c13]. Trump attributed the war to a personality problem between Zelenskyy and Putin [c5]. Trump said that both leaders truly hate each other [c5].

A July study by the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimates the war has cost Russia around 450,000 lives [c6]. The same study estimates that Ukraine has suffered between 125,000 and 150,000 fatalities [c6]. Russian strikes continued in other parts of Ukraine overnight [c16, c17]. An assault on the Odesa region killed one person and injured five others, including a child [c16]. Overnight strikes in the Dnipro region killed two police officials [c17].

vocab.meaning: responds to an action with a similar action
things that are given up to reach an agreement

stories.headline: UN General Assembly votes to adopt new world map accurately representing Africa's size
stories.body:
The UN General Assembly voted 164 to 1 to adopt a resolution replacing traditional world maps with a new map [c18]. The resolution, named Correct the Map, adopts a map projection that accurately represents the size of Africa [c18]. Six countries abstained from the vote [c18]. The United States was the only country to vote against the resolution [c19]. US representative Yaryna Ferencevych criticized the resolution [c23]. Ferencevych said that debating 16th-century map projects instead of international peace mocked the General Assembly's purpose [c23].

The traditional Mercator map shows Africa as similar in size to Greenland [c20]. In reality, Africa is 14 times larger than Greenland [c20]. African Union member states and the Bahamas sponsored the resolution [c24]. The resolution is non-legally binding and does not challenge using the Mercator map for sea and air navigation [c25].

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced that his ministry will stop using the Mercator map [c22]. Barrot said at Sorbonne University that the Mercator map gives the US, Russia, and China disproportionate visual prominence over Africa, Latin America, or Southeast Asia [c28]. France plans to switch to the Eckert IV map projection [c29]. Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey said that Togo hopes to transition school geography materials away from the Mercator map by the end of the year [c26].

vocab.meaning: a way of representing the curved surface of the Earth on a flat map
the state of being noticeable or important

stories.headline: Reform UK aides resign amid investigations into alleged election law and donation breaches
stories.body:
Two senior advisers to Reform UK leader Nigel Farage stepped down after an undercover investigation into political polling [c33]. Advisers James Orr and Dan Jukes resigned after an investigation alleged Reform UK arranged foreign-funded polling [c33]. The investigation by group Verbatim was broadcast on Channel 4 [c35]. It alleged Reform UK arranged for a US company to pay over £30,000 for three opinion polls [c35].

James Orr served as Reform UK's head of policy since February and works as an associate professor of divinity at the University of Cambridge [c39]. US Vice President JD Vance previously referred to Orr as his intellectual mentor [c44]. In undercover footage, Orr was recorded saying Farage does not know and will not know about the poll funding arrangement [c45]. Orr said the polling was paid for by an independent person and denied it benefited the party [c36]. Cambridge announced it is looking into Orr's conduct [c40].

Undercover footage also showed Farage meeting fake US donors over lunch in Clacton [c41]. Farage described the investigation as entrapment and called the claims loose pub talk [c42]. Farage was also heckled by protesters at the party's conference in Birmingham on Friday [c32]. The Labour Party asked the Metropolitan Police to investigate potential criminal funding offences [c34].

vocab.meaning: the act of tricking someone into committing a crime
the study of religion and theology

stories.headline: Escalating clashes between Houthis and Yemeni government forces leave dozens dead in western Yemen
stories.body:
Houthi forces launched a ground offensive on Thursday against coalition forces supporting Yemen's government-in-exile [c46]. The offensive targeted Saudi Arabia-led coalition forces in western Yemen [c46]. An AFP tally reported that 129 people have died in the renewed fighting as of Friday [c47]. A Houthi source said that more than 100 fighters from both sides have died since the attack began [c52].

Heavy shelling and artillery fire forced hundreds of families to flee from the coastal cities of Hodeidah and Mokha [c48]. The Houthis are seeking control of ports and high ground near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait [c49]. The strait connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden [c49].

Yemeni government forces recaptured the al-Khazan and al-Makahna hills west of Taiz city [c50]. State television reported that a ballistic missile attack on a restaurant in al-Makha killed several civilians and injured others [c51]. The Houthis previously controlled al-Makha before government forces and the Saudi-led coalition drove them out in 2017 [c53].

vocab.meaning: a narrow passage of water connecting two larger bodies of water

stories.headline: US diesel prices hit record high amid energy market disruptions from Iran conflict
stories.body:
Average US diesel prices reached a record high of $5.85 per gallon on Friday [c54]. According to AAA, this price surpassed the previous record of $5.81 set in June 2022 [c60]. US diesel prices have increased by about 55% since the US-Israeli conflict with Iran began on February 28 [c55]. On that date, the national average was $3.76 a gallon [c55]. The average price of regular gasoline reached $4.15 per gallon, up from $2.98 before the war [c59].

Brent crude oil was trading above $95 a barrel on Friday, compared to around $70 before the conflict [c56]. Distillate inventories on the US East Coast fell to a record low of 19.3 million barrels in late August [c57]. About 90% of US school buses run on diesel fuel [c61]. Russia also restricted diesel exports through September 30 after Ukrainian drones attacked Russian oil refineries [c58].

US President Donald Trump announced an oil agreement with Venezuela to lower fuel prices [c62]. Venezuelan Interim President Delcy Rodríguez said the deal involves developing 17 oil fields [c64]. A poll showed Trump's approval rating dropped to 33%, with 31% approving of the Iran war [c65].

a refined liquid product obtained from petroleum

stories.headline: Rescue operations continue in Nepal floods as Indian nationals remain missing and workers saved from tunnel
stories.body:
Rescuers pulled two workers alive from a flooded hydropower tunnel in Nepal after massive flash floods [c76, c85]. Preliminary investigations show a collapsed glacier and its bedrock triggered a flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border [c73, c77]. Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said the floods were caused by an ice-rock avalanche [c85].

Nepalese authorities reported at least 1,295 people were killed in the disasters [c82]. More than 12,000 people have been rescued across Nepal, while almost 5,000 people remain missing [c83]. Local authorities reported that floods damaged 35 motorable bridges, 45 suspension bridges, and 40 kilometers of black-topped roads in central Nepal [c84]. A massive landslide occurred at Bhattar in Api Himal Rural Municipality [c87]. The landslide partially blocked the Chaulani River in Darchula district [c87]. The Chaulani River flows into the Mahakali River along the Nepal-India border [c88].

The flash floods severely impacted Nepal's power sector [c68]. Almost 100% of Nepal's electricity comes from hydropower [c66]. The floods severely damaged 12 hydropower plants in the Trishuli River basin [c68]. The destruction knocked out more than 10% of Nepal's total power generation capacity [c68]. The state-owned Nepal Electricity Authority owns six of the 12 damaged facilities [c69]. The Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project was valued at about $647 million before being nearly destroyed [c75]. Overall, Nepal has 225 hydropower plants with over 3,900 megawatts of installed capacity [c71]. The country earns nearly $200 million each year exporting hydroelectricity to India and Bangladesh [c67]. In 2010, only two-thirds of Nepal's population had electricity access [c70].

Climate factors have contributed to increasing hazards in the region [c72, c74]. High-altitude Himalayan regions are warming 50% faster than the global average [c72]. According to disaster authorities, more than nine in 10 recorded disaster events in Nepal between 2018 and 2024 were climate-related [c74].

The Indian government has engaged in relief and recovery efforts [c80, c81]. India's Ministry of External Affairs reported that 275 Indian nationals remain missing after the floods [c77]. A total of 166 Indian nationals were rescued, and 1,907 Indian nationals safely crossed into Nepal from China [c78, c79]. India supplied about 95 tonnes of relief material using seven aircraft [c80]. India also deployed 54 personnel to Nepal, including 30 tunnel rescue experts, 19 forensic experts, and a five-member medical team [c81]. In India, the Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority designated Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital in Bengaluru as the center to collect DNA samples from relatives of missing persons [c86].

vocab.meaning: the maximum amount that something can produce or contain
relating to scientific tests or techniques used in investigation

stories.headline: Air India sacks pilot after drug test confirmation following total hydraulics failure on Phuket-Delhi flight
stories.body:
Air India dismissed a pilot who tested positive for a psychoactive substance after an inflight emergency [c93]. The pilot commanded an August 4 flight from Phuket to Delhi carrying 137 passengers and crew members [c89, c93, c102]. The eight-year-old Airbus A320neo aircraft suffered a near-simultaneous loss of all three hydraulic systems at 36,000 feet [c89]. The flight control system detected the loss of the green hydraulic system at 9:32 am, followed four seconds later by the loss of the blue and yellow systems [c90, c100].

During the altitude upset, the aircraft gained 372 feet and dropped by 292 feet [c91]. The blue hydraulic system was restored shortly after 9:32 am, followed by the yellow and green systems [c101]. The aircraft landed safely at Delhi airport at 11:00 am IST [c103]. At least 24 people received medical assistance, with at least four suffering serious injuries [c97].

Both pilots passed alcohol breath analyzer tests in Delhi [c94]. But a confirmatory blood test returned a non-negative result for a psychoactive substance for the pilot-in-command [c95]. The co-pilot tested negative [c95]. The pilot-in-command was monitoring controls rather than flying during the incident [c99]. Under civil aviation rules, pilots testing positive must undergo rehabilitation before flying again [c96]. Air India said safety is its highest priority [c98].

vocab.meaning: operated by liquid moving under pressure
affecting the mind or mental processes

stories.headline: Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj detained over alleged assault on protester's father at Jantar Mantar
stories.body:
Police in Uttar Pradesh took Hindutva influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj into custody after an assault investigation [c107, c113]. Bhardwaj was detained in Bulandshahr [c107]. The detention came after a July 23 attack at Jantar Mantar during youth protests against exam irregularities [c113]. Dalit activist Nishu Aazad's father, Sanjay Kumar, was injured in the attack [c105, c113].

In a podcast, Bhardwaj claimed he cracked Kumar's skull and said the injury required 60 stitches [c109]. Bhardwaj claimed that he acted in self-defence after 10 to 15 people surrounded him [c110]. In a viral video, Bhardwaj claimed a phone call from Delhi minister Kapil Mishra helped him avoid arrest [c114]. Bhardwaj also made anti-Muslim statements during a podcast on September 1 [c116]. He said he wants to form a hardline Hindu party to create a Muslim-free India [c117].

The Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) filed a police complaint against Bhardwaj for falsely claiming an association with Union minister Chirag Paswan [c106]. Paswan said he takes full responsibility for pursuing the matter with Delhi Police to ensure justice [c108]. Cockroach Janta Party members protested outside Parliament Street police station demanding attempt-to-murder charges [c115]. Bhardwaj was also booked under the POCSO Act on September 4 after allegedly threatening a minor activist [c119].

vocab.meaning: the act of keeping someone in official custody
actions that do not follow official rules or standards
